subject: Sprint-zero: NovaClinic on‑prem cluster intake — hardware/profile questions

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Sprint-zero: NovaClinic on-prem cluster intake — hardware/profile questions

James —

Thanks for the intake packet you sent this morning. Before we lock in the Site Prep checklist and the on-site staging window, the infra team at Redwood needs a few clarifications so we can size node pools and storage profiles properly for the initial deployment. High‑level asks below — short answers are fine, we can dive deeper on the call next week.

1) Rack & networking: you mentioned two racks in the doc. Are both racks cabled into the same L2/L3 leaf pair (single network fabric), or are they in separate zones with cross‑connects? Any dedicated BGP/MPLS or firewall appliances we need to know about?

2) Persistent store: the inventory lists a NetApp FAS cluster for primary storage. Can we get the storage protocol (NFSv3/NFSv4/SMB/iSCSI) and whether multipath is enabled?

3) Local NVMe: you flagged local NVMe on the inference nodes as "ephemeral cache" — what size per node will be available (GB) and are they presented as raw NVMe or LVM-managed?

4) Encryption & KMS: confirmation that keys are customer‑managed via your KMS (we noted a HSM integration) and whether we should expect per‑volume CMKs or a single cluster key.

5) Workload profile: expected steady‑state concurrent inference QPS and burst QPS for the first quarter (ballpark is fine). Also retention requirements for model artifacts and logs (SLA/retention days).

If you prefer, we can convert these into a short preflight form and send to you. Our recommended next steps: obtain the storage protocol details and NVMe sizing so Karthik and I can produce a node‑pool + PV class proposal.

Cheers,

Markus Klein
Head, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sprint-zero: NovaClinic on-prem cluster intake — hardware/profile questions

Markus — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline below; attaching the site inventory CSV and our storage topology diagram.

1) Racks/network: both racks sit in the same L2 fabric and connect to dual leaf switches (redundant). We have a downstream firewall appliance (FortiGate) at the aggregation layer for east-west segmentation — you can expect NAT for outbound egress through our perimeter.

2) Persistent store: NetApp FAS exposed via NFSv4.1 export to the app VLAN; multipath is handled on the filer side. We plan to expose mount points to the Kubernetes nodes for CSI NFS usage.

3) Local NVMe: primary inference nodes will have 2 x 3.84TB NVMe each, presented as raw devices. We plan to reserve ~1.5TB per node for inference KV cache; rest can be used for local scratch.

4) Encryption & KMS: keys managed in our HSM (Entrust). We expect per‑volume data encryption; we can provide wrap/unwrapping flow. For now assume CMKs per cluster.

5) Workload: our pilot will start light — steady state ~120 concurrent inference threads, with bursts to ~800 for short windows (10–15 minutes) during peak scanning cycles. Model artifacts retention: 90 days. Logs: 365 days archived to our S3 equivalent.

We have a compliance audit scheduled July 18 — if you can provide the preflight checklist and a recommended nodepool sizing before then, that would be ideal.

James / team — great context, thanks. Based on the answers and our runbook, here are concrete recommendations we think will meet the pilot profile and compliance window. I'll keep this high level; we can turn into a technical decision record afterwards.

Node pools (recommendation):
- control-plane (3 masters, no GPU): 3 x m5‑equivalent (8 vCPU / 32GB) — tainted -NoSchedule for user workloads.
- infra (storage, logging, monitoring): 3 x 16v / 64GB nodes with 6TB HDD/SATA (or thin LUNs on NetApp) for long retention volumes; provision PVs with Retain policy for artifacts.
- inference-gpu (production): start with 6 nodes x A40-equivalent (or your GPU equivalent), each with 2 x 3.84TB NVMe local devices. Use a DaemonSet for the NVMe local-cache manager to expose one device as /var/lib/redwood/cache (size limit: 1.5TB).

Storage classes and PV strategy:
- CSI NFS (NetApp): create a ReadWriteMany class for shared config/state (k8s config exports, model repo pointers).
- Block PVs for model weights and stateful components backed by NetApp LUNs (Retain/PVC resize enabled).
- Local PVs for KV cache on NVMe (StorageClass local-static) with ephemeral reclaim policy (Delete).
- Snapshot/backup: enable CSI snapshots and automated transfers to your S3 target (retention rules as you specified).

Network/egress:
- Egress through your firewall will require explicit NAT/port allowances for Redwood health/probe endpoints (we will provide IPs).
- Enable topology aware volume provisioning (topology.kubernetes.io/zone) — although on single fabric this is still useful for future multi‑rack zoning.

Kubelet and eviction settings:
- evictionHard: memory.available<300Mi,nodefs.available<10%
- enable kubelet local storage isolation; set node lease TTL to 40s for faster failure detection.

Security & KMS:
- integrate with your HSM for volume encryption keys; we will support per‑namespace CMK mapping.

Next steps I propose (short timeline):
- Today: Redwood sends a preflight with IPs and port list + short nodepool BOM (we will attach nodeprofile-recommendations.xlsx).
- Tomorrow: quick 30m sync to confirm device mapping and NetApp export paths.
- By EOD Jul 17: we will deliver a finalized node pool + PV class proposal for procurement.

I'll attach a trimmed checklist for the infra team — Markus, please add any commercial/contract asks before we send it to James.

— Karthik
